This step is indicated by a rectangle with a curved arrow pointing downwards. G6P is then converted into fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) by the enzyme phosphoglucose isomerase, as shown by a curved arrow pointing to the right. This step is represented by a circle with a curved arrow pointing to the right. The two three-carbon molecules are then converted into 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (1,3BPG) and 3-phosphoglycerate (3PG) through a series of enzymatic reactions, illustrated by a series of curved arrows pointing downwards and to the right. Finally, 3PG is converted into pyruvate, which can be further metabolized in the mitochondria or used to generate ATP through substrate-level phosphorylation.
